#### 1. amyloidosis, hereditary systemic 6  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.500)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2424491, Reactome:R-HSA-9705671, Reactome:R-HSA-1236977, Reactome:R-HSA-877300, Reactome:R-HSA-9637628)

**Proposed mechanism:** Beta-2-microglobulin (B2M) (HGNC:914) —DECREASES→ Decreased B2M protein levels (HP:0003128); Beta-2-microglobulin (B2M) (HGNC:914) —PRODUCES→ Amyloidogenic B2M variants; Amyloidogenic B2M variants —LEADS_TO→ Amyloid deposition (HP:0003214). Loss-of-function mutations in B2M lead to hypoproteinemia by decreasing overall B2M protein levels. Gain-of-function mutations in B2M lead to the production of amyloidogenic variants, which deposit as amyloid and cause hereditary systemic amyloidosis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in B2M associated with hypoproteinemia, hypercatabolic that are not loss-of-function, or variants associated with amyloidosis, hereditary systemic 6 that are not gain-of-function. _(variant: Any common variants (AF > 0.001) in HGNC:914 that are not associated with either disease phenotype.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the dual role of B2M in both loss-of-function and gain-of-function disease mechanisms could inform therapeutic strategies targeting protein stability or degradation pathways for related proteinopathies.

#### 2. RASopathy  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.439)

Loss-of-function mutations in B2M can disrupt protein homeostasis, potentially affecting pathways like MAPK signaling and contributing to hypoproteinemia. Gain-of-function mutations in MAPK pathway genes like PTPN11 cause RASopathies. Both disease chains converge on the MAPK signaling pathway, albeit through different functional consequences.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that B2M mutations do not impact the MAPK signaling pathway or that genes causing RASopathies do not converge on any shared downstream effectors with protein metabolism dysregulation. _(variant: rs112606813 (B2M p.Val72Met) with an allele frequency >0.01 in gnomAD.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding this overlap could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting the MAPK pathway for both protein metabolism disorders and RASopathies, potentially improving treatment efficacy and broadening patient benefit.

Dysregulation of these pathways can manifest as distinct phenotypes, including hypoproteinemia, hypercatabolic, and epidermal nevi.

**How to falsify it:** Absence of gain-of-function mutations in HRAS, NRAS, PIK3CA, or FGFR3 in individuals with hypoproteinemia, hypercatabolic, or epidermal nevus would falsify this hypothesis.
